Start with what it isn't. It isn't a constant like the Halving — nothing about it is provable, measurable, or repeatable, and nobody has ever produced an equation for it the way the Long Chapter did for entropy. It isn't a mass like the Singularity, either — there's no gravity well, no boundary anyone could plot a course toward or away from. What channelers describe, when they describe anything at all, isn't a place or a thing. It's a direction. Beyond the Triangle, beyond even Faith — the Reckoner's own pillar names it more literally than anyone realized when they wrote it down: a border reality has, that the Outside sits past, not inside.

Accounts never corroborate. Two Reckoners describing the same channeling session will disagree, point-blank, on basic geometry — one says the space folded inward, the other insists it opened outward, and both are certain. Nobody agrees on how much time passed while they were channeling it; five minutes and forty-five minutes have both been reported for the same working, by people standing in the same room. Whatever obeys this world's physics clearly doesn't include whatever the Outside actually is.

That disagreement is the closest thing to evidence anyone has. The Halving is constant, provable, math — every account matches because everyone's measuring the same equation. The Singularity is a real astronomical category, even if this particular instance sits unreachably far off — everyone at least agrees on what kind of thing it is. Nobody has ever produced two independent accounts of the Outside that agree on basic facts. A convincing lie is usually more consistent than that. The disagreement itself, oddly, is the strongest evidence anyone has that there's something real out there to disagree about.
